coldOpenOptions.title: Purana Qila, in layers
coldOpenOptions.tagline: A cut through the ground. Oldest at the bottom.

taglineEvidence.text: The layer below this seals the structures of the Sultanate Period.
Below these layers are successive structures of the Rajput, Post-Gupta, Gupta, Kushan, Sunga, and Mauryan Periods in the adjoining excavated areas.
Below the Pre-Mauryan levels was found a significant silt deposit
The layer through which the Mauryan ring well cuts through, i.e., the Pre-Mauryan levels
the natural soil has not yet been reached
comprising mixed material of various periods

coldOpenOptions.taglineNote: Layer order only: P1 lists each period below the later one, and the silt below the Pre-Mauryan levels. Cut features (ring well, drain, pits, the modern controlled pit) reach into older layers and stay drawn as cuts. The base is the oldest layer shown, not natural soil, which has not been reached. Modern fill holds older objects but is the latest deposit. “A cut” names the view, a section through the ground; the end card states that it is composite.
